entities.name: RBP4
observations: Circulating serum RBP4 increased with the number of narrowed coronary vessels and independently correlated with CAD severity in 305 angiographically proven CAD patients; β=0.297, severity model R²=0.422, p<0.001 (PMID:25142320).
Serum RBP4 positively correlated with Gensini score (r=0.286, p=0.034) and SYNTAX I score (r=0.403, p=0.002) in 55 ACS patients (PMID:34616228).
In subclinical hypothyroidism, serum RBP4 increased with stenosed-vessel number and positively correlated with Gensini score among patients with CAD (PMID:31278889).

In STEMI patients, SYNTAX score correlated positively with RBP4 in double-vessel disease (r=0.616) and three-vessel disease (r=0.423), both p<0.05; vessel-group RBP4 differences were not significant (PMID:33198863).
Evidence is observational, heterogeneous, and not uniformly adjusted; clinical evidence supports association with lesion burden but not causality or specific plaque vulnerability.

entities.name: Coronary artery disease
observations: Circulating RBP4 is positively associated with angiographic lesion burden/severity across studies using Gensini score, SYNTAX score, and number of diseased or stenosed vessels (PMID:25142320; PMID:31278889; PMID:34616228; PMID:33198863).
The evidence is observational and supports biomarker association rather than causation; no convincing evidence specifically establishes association with plaque vulnerability morphology.

entities.name: PMID:25142320
observations: Human angiographic study of 305 CAD patients and 91 controls; serum RBP4 increased with narrowed-vessel number and independently correlated with CAD severity.

entities.name: PMID:34616228
observations: Human ACS study reporting positive serum RBP4 correlations with Gensini and SYNTAX I scores.

entities.name: PMID:31278889
observations: Subclinical hypothyroidism cohort reporting higher serum RBP4 with CAD, more stenosed vessels, and higher Gensini score.

entities.name: PMID:33198863
observations: STEMI cohort reporting positive RBP4-SYNTAX correlations in double- and three-vessel disease, without significant RBP4 differences across vessel-number groups.
